analysis.evidence: וּמַלְכִּי צֶדֶק gives the full name. The following title מֶלֶךְ שָׁלֵם, “king of Salem,” identifies Melchizedek as the man who brought out bread and wine.
analysis.morphology: צֶדֶק is the second component of a Hebrew personal name. The marked token has no prefix or suffix.
Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מֶלֶךְ שָׁלֵם, “king of Salem,” מֶלֶךְ is in construct, and שָׁלֵם names the city in Melchizedek’s title.
analysis.morphology: Unprefixed proper noun with no suffix.

analysis.evidence: Melchizedek, king of Salem, is the subject. The direct objects לֶחֶם וָיָיִן name what he brought out, bread and wine.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with Melchizedek.

analysis.evidence: Melchizedek brought out לֶחֶם וָיָיִן, “bread and wine.” The two nouns name the specific provisions he brought.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of common gender, singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Melchizedek brought out לֶחֶם וָיָיִן ‘bread and wine’. The verb הוֹצִיא takes both nouns as its objects, pairing wine with bread as provisions.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וָ־ ‘and’ prefixes יָיִן, the pausal form of the masculine singular absolute noun יַיִן.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69133:5, 69132:9, 66320:13.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces a background clause. הוּא is an independent third-person masculine singular pronoun.

analysis.evidence: In וְהוּא כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן, הוּא refers to Melchizedek, כֹהֵן names his office, and לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן identifies the God he serves.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן identifies Melchizedek as a priest of God Most High. עֶלְיוֹן qualifies אֵל, the deity he serves.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks whom the priest serves. אֵל is a masculine singular noun in the absolute state, modified by עֶלְיוֹן.

analysis.evidence: כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן describes Melchizedek as a priest of God Most High. Here עֶלְיוֹן follows אֵל and serves as a divine epithet.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective modifying אֵל, with no prefix or suffix.
